reviews.text: 🌸 Peaceful Escape in the Heart of Beijing — Jingshan Park (景山公园) ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5) I recently visited Jingshan Park in Beijing, China — and absolutely loved the place! 🌿 🏞️ Beautiful Scenery: The park is surrounded by green trees, colorful flowers, and traditional Chinese pavilions. It’s clean, calm, and full of natural beauty. ⏰ Short but Sweet Visit: Our tour company allowed only a short stay, so we couldn’t climb to the top of the hill. Still, even from the lower level, the park looked amazing and offered great photo spots. 💭 Impression: It’s peaceful, well-maintained, and perfect for a relaxing walk or photography. The atmosphere is truly refreshing — you can feel both nature and culture blending together. 📸 Photos: I’ve uploaded some of my favorite pictures — hope you enjoy them as much as I enjoyed the visit! ✨ Next Time: I’ll definitely hike up to the hilltop to see the panoramic view of Beijing city. Highly recommended for anyone visiting Beijing!

Beautiful view and relaxing place! I visited Jingshan Park in the evening and it was quite crowded, but totally worth it. The walk up the hill isn’t too steep, and once you reach the top, the view is absolutely stunning — you can see the entire Forbidden City stretched out right in front of you. The golden sunset over the rooftops makes it even more magical. It’s a perfect spot for photos, relaxing, or just taking a quiet moment above the busy city. Even with many visitors, the park still feels peaceful and full of history. Highly recommend visiting around sunset for the best atmosphere!

A lovely park, very well maintained. It gets a bit busy - but that’s China. Costs 2 RMB for entry so basically nothing. The main attraction is the temple on the hill and the views over the entire Forbidden City.

Jingshan Park is one of Beijing’s most historic and scenic spots. Famous as the site where the last Ming emperor tragically ended his life, the park today is a peaceful green space that offers some of the best panoramic views of the Forbidden City. Climbing the hill is not difficult, and from the top pavilion you’re rewarded with a sweeping perspective of the imperial palace’s golden rooftops stretching out in perfect symmetry. On clear days, the view is truly breathtaking and one of the best places to capture the scale of old Beijing.

Consider doing in this format, Tiananmen square->Tiananmen->Forbidden city->Jing shan park. Walk from South to North, where the Jingshan park is located. It is a very easy 10 min walk up to the top and you get a panaromic view of the whole Forbidden city.

A perfect place to go if you want to have whole view of Imperial Palace. I came here in the morning, not too crowded. But somebody told me it will be better in the afternoon when the afternoon sun shines on its golden roof.

Lovely park with lots of walking paths. Take the one "uphill" and it will take you to the Wanchun Pavilion (c. 1750) at the top. Great views in all directions and a great place to see the size of the Forbidden City.

A well maintained, beautiful park right outside of the forbidden city the artificial hill is both the geographic center of imperial Beijing and an excellent place for views of the forbidden city there is a nominal fee to enter the grounds that amounts to less than one dollar.

This is a park where you can get bird eye view of the Forbidden Palace. You can access by buying ticket costing 2 yuan. There is an easy uphill walk to the Wanchun Palace where you take 360 degree view of beijing, which include the Forbidden city

September 2025 5* Famous park in Beijing to get the top view of Forbidden city and Beijing skyline. The park is very nice and you need to climb stairs to reach high point. Compare to other park, this remains open till 8 pm and you can get good night view from the top. There is 360 deck so you can see forbidden city on one side and city view on the other side.
Great park to visit especially as the Forbidden Palace requires advanced tickets. You get a great view of the palace from up high.

Beautiful view of Jingshan Park from the courtyard outside the Gate of Divine Prowess (神武门) with the Wanchun Pavilion (万春亭) standing on top of the hill. A great spot to pause & take in the scenery before ending the tour to the Forbidden City.
Beautiful park with lots of history. There's a viewpoint of the city at the top of the hill. However it can be a little crowded at the top. And IMO the nearby beihai park is a lot prettier.

I arrived 5ish, getting tickets on the spot is a breeze. Crowded but not as bad as other touristy spots. With patience and persistence you will surely get a spot to take scenic pics. I’m short in statute so can’t say my vantage point is ideal. Spotted two resident cat, one of which seemed to be zzz on the job 😂 all in all I spent 20 mins or so in the park as it was getting dark. All in all, it’s a Rmb2 well spent
My wife and I had the opportunity to transit in Beijing for 24 hours. We managed to take a glimpse of the Forbidden City from d peak of the park. The entrance fee is only 4 yuan

Nice park with a short hill (< 5 mins to climb up) to enjoy the magnificent view of the forbidden palace. Easy hike. There are a couple of exhibitions at the base park as well. Avoid during peak season or holidays.

A beautiful park where you can just stroll among the flowers, or go up to several point views, which offer a good view of the Forbidden City and Beijing itself. A lot of beautiful local girls come to take videos and photos in national costumes - we even saw very small children, they looked very cute. It’s great when people cherish their history and culture. There are much fewer people than in the Forbidden City itself. And the ticket costs only 2 yuans per an adult.
Very nice park to view the whole 故官' palace . Entry fee was cheap. Must go if you in Beijing
A little hilltop overlooking the forbidden city, apart from the view, it is also the central point of Beijing city and where the last Ming emperor ended his life.

If you didn't get an appointment to get into Tianamen Square or the Forbidden City and want to overlook both, this is the place to come. Go early in the morning because it gets crowded at the top temple. If you want to just check out the place, they have multiple temples you can get into and enjoy the scenery. Definitely worth a stop!

A great hike up the hill to see a perfect view of the forbidden place museum. It was super crowded during a public holiday so getting a photo might be difficult if there is a lot of people but still worth the visit. Didn’t need to pre book tickets and tickets are super cheap.
It’s the 100th anniversary of the Palace Museum this year. It’s cool to see the whole of the palace from a different angle. Absolutely stunning.

If you're looking for the best aerial view of the Palace Museum, Jingshan Park is the place to go! Conveniently accessible via the Beijing metro. The highlight of Jingshan Park is undoubtedly the panoramic view from the top of Jingshan Hill. The golden rooftops of the Forbidden City stretch out majestically before you, creating a breathtaking sight. I highly recommend visiting during sunrise or sunset when the lighting adds a magical touch to the scene. Jingshan Park is a must-visit spot in Beijing.

Please note that google maps in China does not work. in the park you can climb to a small elevation and have a very nice view of the forbidden city. the pavilion on the height is located in an axis with the largest and most famous sights of Beijing city center.

Amazing park with great views of Beijing and the Forbidden City. Right behind the Forbidden City so you should visit after if you can Very short hike to the peak Tickets can be purchased online or in person for 2 yuan

Nicely maintained park. However, its main attraction of course awaits a short hike up the hill... wide open views of Beijing and the Forbidden City. There is also a plaque on top of the hill marking the 'Central Point of Beijing City'.

Climb one hill, see all of Beijing — not a bad deal. Jingshan Park is basically the VIP balcony to the Forbidden City. After wandering through centuries of imperial drama, hike up here for the perfect panoramic payoff. The view is chef’s kiss, especially at sunset. You’ll feel like the emperor surveying his kingdom… or at least like a tourist with great cardio. Bonus points: fewer crowds, more trees, and zero palace politics. Totally worth the leg burn.

If you are unable to get tickets into Forbidden City, Jingshan Park is a good way to see it from far. There are multiple levels if you go up where you can see the Forbidden City and you can see how huge it actually is. It is a gorgeous park with many beautiful trees. Highly recommended for a visit!

Beautifully maintained gardens right next to the Forbidden City. Entry is cheap and you don't need to buy tickets in advance. Lots of bus access close to the entry gates. Most people come here because it overlooks the FC but if you're planning on getting shots of the FC lit up at night, a security guard told us that they only do that on Friday, Saturday, and public holidays. Be warned, no matter what day you go, you will be fighting for the good photo spots at the top with hordes of young women taking a bazillion selfies and jerks with tripods taking up enough space for several people. You can actually get some really nice sunset shots of Bai Ha (Beihai Park) just around the other side of the pagoda so be sure to keep your eyes open all the other sights this park has to offer.
A vantage point for the stunning panoramic view of the Central Axis. Best to either come early in the morning or near sunset.

Jingshan Park is conveniently located just across the exit of the Forbidden City. Although it requires a bit of an uphill climb with stairs, the marvelous view of the Forbidden City from the top is well worth the effort. I highly recommend visiting this park. There are four entrances to the park: north, south, west, and east.

The royal hill garden north of the imperial palace. A good vantage point to oversee the palace. Came on a Sunday and it is sure crowded. It’s good if you have a good camera for distant shots else with an iPhone, the photos dun really look great. It’s a must come attraction in Beijing. I feel in snow, the palace photos will definitely look great shooting from this height.

Superb place to visit and see some wonderful panoramic views of Beijing - especially of the Forbidden City. The hill represents the "mountain" to be positioned behind a property (with a lake / river at the front) as per Feng Shui principles. The earth excavated from the moat surrounding the Forbidden City was used to build this mountain. It's an easy climb of around 200 steps to the top.

After visiting the Forbidden City this is the perfect end to the day - walking up the slight hill to look back on the wonder you have just experienced. Like everything in Beijing you need a ticket, but it's cheap and amazingly you can buy it at the gate. There may be several gates, but we entered from the east side, about halfway up Jingshan East street. The park is nice to wander, but you'll want to head up the path to the viewing area. It's not too hard, but after miles of walking already you might struggle. There's not much space at the top, so be prepared to wait and then rugby scrum your way into any spot to get a view. Despite the usual terrible Chinese queuing etiquette, I was floored here by kindness. I asked a Chinese lady, who had somehow nabbed the perfect spot, if she minded me standing nearby to take a picture. She'd probably waited all day to get the spot, but she got up and offered me the seat! I gave it back immediately after taking a few photographs, of course. Obviously the big draw for this park are the views of the forbidden city, but the hillside park also has other great vistas, like the capital city's grand skyscrapers.

Amazing park behind the Forbidden City, with a hill full of traditional buildings on it, from where you can get amazing views of Beijing (to all its cardinal points), and in particular of the Forbidden City. You can also see beautiful sunsets, so I suggest visiting in late afternoon/evening.

This park north of the Forbidden City features an artificial hill providing some great views, as there are not any high rise buildings to the south you get a nearly unbroken view to the skyline. From this vantage point you can see how truely massive (and crowded) the Forbidden City is. It's a nice place to relax, and enjoy a spot of nature in the middle of the city.

Nice and scenic park with lots of ginkgo trees by the side. It is a short climb up the hill for excellent views of the Palace grounds. To access the park from the Palace Museum, take the underground pedestrian pass and enter through a ticketing counter. We didn’t have to get tickets to Jingshan Park in advance, and they cost just about 2 Chinese yuan.
very touristy city in China with a lake for wooden boat rides and on the shores of the lake tourist shops with the usual tourist products! And snacks of roasted cockroaches, worms and other insects 😁

Excellent place to have a walk and have a view of Beijing city particularly the Forbidden City. This is not a natural hill. It was built after one of the emperors complained about the cold air blowing from the north. Hence a hill with trees was created to block the winter winds.
Entrance fee is 2 yuan, the park closes at 8:30 pm so you can visit at night, on the hill you can see the Forbidden City and the surrounding area very beautifully.
Must visit park with a fantastic view over the forbidden city. Have to purchase ticket for entrance and do expect long queue over the weekend of long holiday in China.

It is just next to the Forbidden City, and you should definitely visit here. The ticket is so cheap, something like 2 or 3 RMB. Local people would come here singing after dinner, and it sounds fantastic. 🤩 such a unique experience. Climb on the top of the mountain; you will see the Forbidden City from the perfect spot! So lovely to visit during the golden hour.

You can have a good view to forbidden city and hutong nearby. The best time to visit here is in the morning, you will see local elders exercise and do fun activities in the park. It’s not touristic during early morning and you see how local people enjoy life and stay fit.

If you are looking for a unique and breathtaking perspective of the Forbidden City, you might want to check out the man-made hill behind it. This artificial mound, known as Jingshan Park, was built from the soil excavated during the construction of the imperial palace. It offers a vantage point to have an unobstructed view of the magnificent complex and its surroundings.

The garden is pretty quiet and beautiful. The best part though is the absolutely breathtaking views of the Fobidden City from the top of the hill (not too long of a walk). It costs ¥2 (chinese yuan) which is nothing. The entrance is right opposite of the north gate of the fobidden city. 100% recommended especially if you didn’t manage to get tickets for the Forbidden City!

Located at the back of the forbidden palace is jingshan park. You can buy tickets on the spot for a small price and get a panoramic view of the forbidden palace below. Recommended to come during sunset when you are done exploring the palace below. It’s quite a few steps up the hill but you are free to rest along the way as the paths are rather wide. Crowds are considered manageable.

One of my favorite parks in Beijing. Like most parks in Beijing, you just pay 2 yuans per person to enter. You’re going to get a great viewpoint of the Forbidden City in this park. Some tour groups skip this park so it’s less crowded compared to the Forbidden City and Beihai park. The best time to go is when the air quality is good in the city, so make sure to check the weather if you want the best experience. When it’s a clear day you can see very far out and it’s so beautiful.

This park was the imperial garden of the Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties. We entered opposite the Shenwu Gate of The Forbidden City. The history is fascinating. The last emperor of the Ming Dynasty (Chongzhen?), hung himself from a locust tree here, as the Invaders were at the gates. The park is manicured to perfection with beautiful colours everywhere in summer. There are also lots of cranes and deer statues scattered around which represent longevity in life. If in anyway fit, you have to scale Jingshan mountain to experience the breathtaking view. They say it takes 20 minutes to get up, and yes it is steep in places, but I jogged up in under 10 minutes no problem. Not only do you have stunning vantage point overlooking the Forbidden City, but if no smog, you also have a 360 view of Beijing and can identify some other landmarks such as the Drum Tower. I really loved my time at this park and could have stayed for hours learning Chinese history along with taking in all that nature.

After visiting the Great Forbidden City, exit from Shenwumen, turn left until you see the underground pedestrian tunnel, and continue along the route until you reach the entrance to Jingshan Park. Purchase a 2 RMB ticket per person and hike to the peak to enjoy the panoramic view of the Forbidden City. The sunset view is stunning.

Beautiful area with great over looking views of the forbidden city. Well worth a visit and it wasn't busy when I was there. There is a lot of small up hill climbs and stairs so might not be the easiest for people with limited mobility.

This was my first stop of the day as I wanted to catch sunrise from here. Sunrise was estimated to be at 7.30am as advised by google, so I made my way up the park at about 7am. It is a short but steep climb up the small hill to reach the vantage point. I recommend coming here for sunrise as compared to sunset as there is significantly lesser people here. In the evenings, the whole place will be flooded with hundreds of photographers and you will find it difficult to take any photographers. Fruthermore its a healthy activity to wake up early and start your day. You are on holiday, so grab the opportunity to start early and visit more attractions. The view is nice and you are able to look down at the entire forbidden palace. The sun rises slightly to the left of the forbidden palace so it may not produce the most spectacular picture, but then again that really depends on the time of the year that you are visiting. Below are some of the pictures that I was able to take when I was here. You are required to purchase a ticket here in order to enter. Unfortunately when I was there, they were not excepting cash. Thankful I had Alipay set up and was able to purchase a ticket that way.

Almost all the tourist places in Beijing are super crowded this one is one of them. When you reached the top you will see the entire Forbidden City but you only need few seconds to see it because many people are waiting to see it too!

Beautiful park to stroll around and it gives great views of the city and the Forbidden city also. Some stairs for climbing so be aware it’s not completely leisurely. People selling drinks inside so you can get water there. Worth the visit and the stroll

For RMB2, this park is probably the best value attraction in Beijing. Grounds are huge, well organized, and full of rich history. Take time to slowly visit the historical buildings within the grounds and savor the centuries of imperial culture. It's a easy climb to the hilltop where you will be rewarded with a view of the Forbidden City and the central axis of Beijing

Despite the official website saying foreigners are supposed to prebook the tickets, it's not correct. It's a hassle to try to buy online as a foreigner. It's definitely easier to just go to the counter and get your tickets on the spot. The view from the top is certainly worry it.

Love this park and the walk up the steps to the temple is a WORK OUT! Make sure to bring walking shoes, water and a camera! Beautiful views once you make it to the top. We went during Chinese New Year and it was pretty crowded.

Nice to see the forsiden city from a view point…. After a long walk in the forsiden city we come out of the North gate and see this parc. So i went up a little climb to see the view of the forbidden city. I was not dissapointed , it was Nice….i also looked to the other side and see the drøm and vell towers.

A beautiful park in the standard Chinese park style. As opposed to European parks a Chinese Park doesn't have straight paths and curves around natural formations, even when the formations aren't natural! This is essentially the mound of dirt and rock from the excavation of the Forbidden City moat. And how glad I am that it exists because the views are amazing. Remember not to be annoying and get in others pictures, take your pictures and leave quickly! It's a quick "hike" (up paved steps) and the view of Beijing and the Forbidden City is well worth it, I recommend a visit after seeing the Forbidden City the same day.

The main point of Jingshan Park is to get a glimpse from afar of the Forbidden City. The trail would be an incline to reach the viewpoint. Prepare your passport and a form of payment such as AliPay or WeChat Pay. Short video to get an idea of what to expect starting at 4:43 - 5.23. https://youtu.be/hZ9MHLyjuoQ

From this park, we can see the whole The Forbidden City. It is famous because of its position, as well as its history. The last ruler of the Ming dynasty, committed suicide by hanging himself from a tree in Jingshan. Prepare your health before walking to its top. You can stand on the center point of Beijing City from this park.
Panoramic arial view of the Forbidden City and less the crazy crowd! Plus point, mere 2RMB entrance ticket! Must-go destination if you are visiting the Forbidden City!

If you still have energy and time after exiting the Forbidden City's north gate, definitely cross the street and check out Jingshan Park. A 15 minute climb up the stairs to the top of the hill offers spectacular 360 degree views of the Forbidden City, Beihai Park, and the Drum and Bell Towers. When the weather is nice walk around the base of the hill and see locals singing, exercising, and playing.

Nice place to get a better idea of the forbidden city size. The entrance fee is only 2 yuan, and the walk to the top is only 15 min. The hill is artificial, as it was made with the ground extracted around the palace to form a square canal.
Very beautiful park allows you to see the forbidden city from up if you couldn’t get ticket to enter

Would say like everyone a must visit place if visiting beijing. Apart from getting the most beautiful view of forbidden City from this you also get to see a lake around. You need to climb some stairs to reach to the top but the view is worth the effort. There is a park around for walking and you need around a day to cover it. If you go on a good weather day you can sit at the peak for the entire day. Very good pics of beijing and the greenery around beijing could be explored from this place.

I thought this place was a hidden gem but I was surprised to see it has more reviews then the Forbidden City. And I can see why, its absolutely beautiful park. An oasis in the hectic mega city of Beijing. Its serene, tranquil and has one of the best views of Beijing when you make the slight trek to the peak of the park. There also seems to be an orchestra of elderly folk who meet here to sing some songs. Its wonderful. I would say this is the top park to visit in Beijing, for sure.

Beautiful views of Beijing and the Forbidden City from the top of the park. Make sure you take the time to walk to the top (will take less than 10 minutes) and visit on a clear day if possible. You’ll then be able to see from all sides of the park, looking down. I preferred the views from the top overlooking the Forbidden City than I did of actually walking around it. There are plenty of locals that use the park, choir singing and playing musical instruments – which is great to see. We got there for sunset, and as you can imagine, it was very crowded and difficult to get the perfect photos you want. But be patient, and you’ll find a space you can slot into eventually.
Park that is opposite the forbidden city. We got our tickets onsite as we do not have a local mainland number to get it on WeChat. Climb up the hill to get a Birds Eye view of the forbidden city!

A short walk to the park from forbidden city.. climbing up to the TOP of a hill .. there are few pavilions along the way and you can chose to stop and rest. The highest one around 47m climb and you would be able to see it clearly the panoramic view of the forbidden city. The park has nothing much rather than having a great view of the forbidden city from the top. Worth a visit if you keen to tale more photo of forbidden city at the elevated land...

Beautiful! Personally prefer it to Forbidden city. You can use your Beijing metro card to enter. Be sure to visit on a clear day if possible! Make sure to climb to the highest spot as there is a rewarding 360 degree view waiting. This park is the site where an emperor hung himself upon losing control of the kingdom to an overthrow.

It's an ancient artificial hill right behind the Forbidden City. If you don't have time, or simply don't want to take on the crowds of the Forbidden City, then visiting this hill is an adequate replacement. It features a nice park combined with probably the best view of the Forbidden City. Entry is 25 CNY (August 2018)

Wonderful place to relax and enjoy Beijing park life. Obviously the view of the Palace Museum and of Beijing from the top is incredible. Better yet is the fun and relaxing atmosphere of the Beijingers enjoying the park themselves. We went on a Monday and the park was filled with dancers, an opera singer, flag twirlers, card players etc. Lots of places to sit and relax. Snack bars for drinks and popcicles. The park itself is absolutely gorgeous and full of trees and flowers. A real gem.

It's so great view point, you can see all of the forbidden city, and the ticket is very cheap only 2 ren min bi per person, walk about few hundred step and you can see whole new view, and I saw some woman practicing some kind of gymnastic practice quite interesting like a local park

360deg splendid view of Beijing skyline from here. Direct view of the Forbidden City. A short climb about 90m with an entrance ticket of rmb2. Good to come by after you have done with the Forbidden City.
Beautiful Park with lots of trees to keep you cool on the hot summer days. Also, if you walk up to the top you can see the Forbidden City.
Charming park, you have a beautiful view of the city up the hill. Must pass by !!
A full view of the Forbidden Palace when not obstructed by jostling crowds. Good crowd management though.

Beautiful and well kept gardens, you're treated to a magnificent view of the Forbidden city and Beijing from the top of a short hike up some stairs to the intricately decorated pavilions. We'll worth a visit. We didn't have time for the forbidden city so was glad we made it to here instead.

Every time you visit forbidden city, walking out of North gate, there you're right in front of Jingshan park. It's another perspective of looking at the giant imperial palace or should I say city, imagining what should've would've could've. Besides, in a clear day you can oversee the whole Beijing in 360 degrees, recognizing lots of iconic places. Who knows you just scan your subway/bus card to get in?! Also you see lots of ppl climbing the hills for exercising. Perfect!

Taking the hike up to the pavilion is worth it after touring the Forbidden City, because you get a first-class view of the place you've been wandering around for the past few hours. Seeing it from this vantage point really drives home how massive the Forbidden City really is. The park is worth it for its own sake too-beautiful pathways with greenery, which is a nice palate cleanser from the Forbidden City. It's also a good place for shade in the hot sun.
Nice views of the forbidden city And Beijing here. To the east of the park there's a lot of Hutongs you can walk through and explore.

UNESCO World Heritage Site Visited Nov 2015 Jingshan Park is an imperial park covering 23 hectares (57 acres) immediately north of the Forbidden City in the Imperial City area of Beijing, China. The focal point is the artificial hill Jingshan. Formerly a private imperial garden attached to the grounds of the Forbidden City, the grounds were opened to the public in 1928.

Jingshan Park is an imperial park covering 23 hectares (57 acres) immediately north of the Forbidden City in the Imperial City area of Beijing, China. The focal point is the artificial hill Jingshan (景山), literally "Prospect Hill". Formerly a private imperial garden attached to the grounds of the Forbidden City, the grounds were opened to the public in 1928. The park was formally established in 1949. It is listed as a Key State Park and is administratively part of Xicheng District in downtown Beijing. The park has a number of attractions and highlights, the most famous of them being the Qiwang Pavilion, the Five Pavilions, the Zhoushang Pavilion, the Guanmiao Pavilion, the Wanchun Pavilion, the Jifang Pavilion, the Fulan Pavilion, the Peony Garden and the Site of Emperor Chongzhen's Suicide.
Nice wiev over the forbidden city. It is clean and preserved park. Good experience after we could not reach forbidden city. And it is for 10 yuan so the price is not so high.

Jingshan Park: translated literally to "Prospect Hill," also known as Coal Hill, is located across the street from the exit of the Forbidden City. The park was a part of the Forbidden City until the early 1900s when the walls were pulled down and a road cut through it, destroying several gates and buildings between the park and the rear entrance of the palace.Just north of the Imperial Palace, the site was a private park reserved for the use of the emperor in the Yuan dynasty (1279-1368). During the Ming dynasty (1368-1644), an artificial hill with five peaks was made, utilizing earth excavated when the moat of the Imperial Palace was dug. This gives the site a unique character, at the top of the hill, the Pavilion of Everlasting Spring, affords stunning, panoramic views over Beijing and the Forbidden City. The park is pleasant to stroll around, popular for locals and visitors alike. It's entertaining to come across groups of elderly Chinese people dancing, singing opera, or doing tai chi even! The hill, can get quite crowded, particularly at sunset on a clear day when many photographers try to catch the last rays of light falling on the rooftops of the Forbidden City. Entrance fee is ¥2 . Closest metro station is Nanluoguxiang station (line 6 or 8).
Relatively small but impressive park tucked behind the Forbidden City - giving the best views of that, and of north Beijing.

Come back in April in order to view the Peonies Show. Local people come every week in during April to see the different type of peonies blooming. It also teaches you how to look for different colour and shape of peonies around the west entry.

A must-see in Beijing! A gorgeous park with lots of history. Be aware that you'll be climbing a lot of stairs. Once you get to the top, there's a phenomenal view of the forbidden city from the back, and a great view of the Beijing skyline.
Nice view of Forbidden City at the top pavilions gardens are OK. Arrange transport as hard to get a taxi on street

Beautiful park. Very clean and well kept park with beautiful natural scenery with planted trees and flowers. One of the main attractions here is watch the elderly people having some leisure time by exercising through dance routines, practicing Chinese calligraphy on the floor with huge brushes dipped in water, or just taking pictures all around them. Another thing you must do is climb the stairs to the top of the park to get a stunning view of the Forbidden City !

One of my favorite places to visit when in Beijing. On a clear day there are great panoramic views of the city and of the forbidden city. If the visibility isn't great this is still a great place to people watch especially on the weekend mornings. The stairs up are not bad at all.

Loved this park amazing views of the Forbidden City and it has amazing temples. Loads of steps though make sure you are physically fit. Great workout though. Really cheap to get in if you go to the city in the morning spend the afternoon here.
we can se gu gong (forbidden city) in here and i have some tips, you can go here when the weather is nice and the sun is set. they said its perfect to see the forbidden city in evening,,
Immediately north of the Forbidden City, this park has a cheap entry ticket and a spectacular view of the surrounding area. Its the best place to view the Forbidden city's true scale.
Historical Chinese temple dated back to 14th century AC in Central Beijing. Amazing historical construction.. Very fortunate to be there thanks to my Chinese friend Jinling ..
Place with very cool overview to forbidden city and other parts of city. Only one disadvantage they take fee for entrance. However, it is regular park.
Decent public park that had a cheap entrance fee. The highest pavilion was overcrowded and honestly not worth walking all that way for in your on a tight timeframes.
we visited at night - beautiful panoramic views of beijing from a different perspective. definitely worth the short climb.
Ticket is 2 RMB, you are able to see the whole view of the forbidden city on the peak of mountain.
Spectacular view , especially during sunset ; Beautiful park, well maintained and safe

Jingshan, also named Coal Hill or Prospect Hill, is a small hill immediately behind the north gate of the Forbidden City. It also borders Beihai Park to the west. Construction of Jingshan dates back 1,000 years ago during the Liao and Jin Dynasties, but the present 43 meters hill was constructed by Emperor Yongle (1360-1424) in the Ming Dyansty. It is also called Coal Hill because large amount of coal used to be put here when the Forbidden City was being built. Built of the soil from the moat of the Forbidden City, the Jingshan Hill used to serve as a private imperial garden and for protecting the Imperial Palace from the evil wind from the north according to Fengshui. It is one of the most important also the highest buildings along the 8 km south-to-north central axis of Beijing. Jingshan was opened to the public in 1928 and a subsequent public park was also established in 1949 which covers 23 hectares. There are five individual peaks in Jingshan and each of them is topped by a beautiful pavilion, which were used by the emperor and officials for gathering and leisure purposes. The biggest pavilion is located on the very top of Jingshan Hill, which is the best location to have a panoramic view of the Forbidden City and downtown Beijing. There were also five copper Buddha statues in each of the pavilion but looted by the Eight Power Allied Forces in 1900. The present five pavilions are actually replicas with a giant Buddha statue in the highest and biggest pavilion. For Chinese people, Jingshan Park is more famous as the place where the last Ming Emperor Chongzhen hung himself in 1644, by the time the peasant revolt army entered Beijing. Right now, it is a popular place with the senior locals for doing morning excise, liking practicing Taichi, singing and dancing. It is also a popular place with the photographers in Beijing to gather in the dust of a clear day, waiting to take a panoramic picture of the Forbidden City with the lights on. There are four entrances to get inside the Jingshan Park; the most convenient one is the south gate which is 100 meters across from the north gate of the Forbidden City. The west entrance is normally used as an exit which is close to the east gate of Beihai, another imperial park nearby.

Jingshan's history dates to the Liao and Jin dynasties, almost a thousand years ago.The 45.7-meter (150 ft) high artificial hill was constructed in the Yongle era of the Ming dynasty entirely from the soil excavated in forming the moats of the Imperial Palace and nearby canals. All of this material was moved by manual labor and animal power. Jingshan consists of five individual peaks, and on the top of each peak there lies an elaborate pavilion. These pavilions were used by officials for gathering and leisure purposes. These five peaks also draw the approximate historical axis of central Beijing. The dictates of feng shui long praised tombs and residences sited south of a nearby hill, serving to channel both harmful yin and cold northern winds. With Jingshan serving that purpose, it gained the name Feng Shui Hill. It is also well known to locals as Coal Hill, from an old rumor that the emperors kept a hidden stash in the park

Parcul Jingshan, situat în inima Beijingului și adiacent Orașului Interzis, este o grădină imperială istorică construită în perioada Yongle a dinastiei Ming. Punctul culminant al parcului este Jingshan, un deal artificial înalt de 45,7 metri, care servește drept cel mai înalt punct al orașului vechi din Beijing. Din Pavilionul Wanchun din vârf, vizitatorii se pot bucura de o vedere panoramică uluitoare asupra Orașului Interzis și a întregului peisaj urban al Beijingului. Parcul găzduiește numeroase flori și copaci rari, ceea ce îl face o destinație perfectă pentru relaxare și vizitarea obiectivelor turistice atât pentru localnici, cât și pentru turiști.

景山公園，這個位於北京城中軸線上的皇家園林，以其深厚的歷史底蘊和優美的自然景觀，成為了遊客探索古都北京的必遊之地。 站在萬春亭上，不僅可以俯瞰故宮的金碧輝煌，還能遠眺北海的白塔，感受京城的古老韻味。 園內的古樹名木，如“母子槐”和“二將軍柏”，見證了歷史的變遷，訴說著往昔的故事。 壽皇殿建築群的修繕，更是讓這座曾經的皇家祭祖場所煥發了新的生命。 無論是春季的牡丹花卉展還是秋季的秋菊展，都展現了景山公園的自然美與文化之韻。 這裡不僅是北京的地理中心，更是文化和歷史的交會點，值得每位遊客細細品味。

好的，这是关于北京景山公园的详细介绍。 景山公园位于中国北京市西城区，坐落在北京中轴线的中心点，故宫的北侧（神武门对面），是元、明、清三代的皇家御苑。它不仅是俯瞰故宫全景和北京城中心风貌的绝佳地点，更是一处承载着深厚历史底蕴的公园。 --- 核心亮点与特色 1. 北京中轴线的制高点 · 景山的主峰“万春亭”高约43米，是北京旧城内的最高点。站在万春亭上，可以向南俯瞰故宫博物院 壮丽的金色琉璃瓦屋顶和层层殿宇，景象极为震撼。向北可以远望钟鼓楼，东西两侧则能看到北海白塔和现代北京的城市风貌。这里是拍摄北京中轴线全景照片的最佳位置。 2. 崇祯皇帝自缢处 · 景山东麓曾有一棵老槐树，是明末崇祯皇帝（朱由检）在1644年李自成起义军攻破北京城时自缢殉国的地方。这给景山增添了一份悲壮的历史色彩。原树已不存在，现在立有碑刻作为历史标记。 3. 五方亭与牡丹文化 · 景山山脊上由五座亭子组成优美的风景线，从东到西依次为：观妙亭、周赏亭、万春亭、富览亭、辑芳亭。这五亭过去供奉着不同的佛像，俗称“五味神”，如今是公园的标志性建筑。 · 公园内种植了大量牡丹，每年4月下旬至5月中旬会举办牡丹节，品种繁多，花色艳丽，是北京著名的牡丹观赏地之一。 4. 绮望楼与寿皇殿 · 绮望楼：位于公园南门内，曾是清代乾隆皇帝供奉孔子牌位的地方。 · 寿皇殿：位于公园北部，是一组规模宏大的建筑群，仿照太庙规制建造，曾是清朝皇帝祭祀祖先的场所。经过精心修缮后现已对公众开放，内部陈设华丽，非常值得一看。 --- 实用游览信息 · 地址：北京市西城区景山西街44号（故宫神武门对面） · 开放时间： · 旺季（4月-10月）：6:00 - 21:00，20:30停止入场 · 淡季（11月-3月）：6:30 - 20:00，19:30停止入场 · 门票价格： · 非常亲民，通常为： · 旺季：成人10元/人 · 淡季：成人2元/人 · 学生、老人等有半价或免费优惠。 · 注意：门票需提前在官方微信公众号“畅游公园”上实名预约购买，尤其是在节假日期间。 · 建议游览时长：2-3小时。 --- 最佳游览路线建议 1. 经典路线（南进北出）： · 从南门进入（正对故宫神武门） → 参观绮望楼 → 开始登山 → 依次游览五方亭，直达最高点万春亭（拍照留念） → 下山后前往寿皇殿建筑群参观 → 从东门或西门离开。 · 这条路线可以完整体验景山的历史和自然景观。 2. 快捷路线： · 如果时间紧张，可以直接从任意门进入，直奔万春亭，俯瞰故宫全景后即可下山。 --- 交通指南 · 公交车：最为方便。可乘坐101路、103路、109路、124路、128路等公交车在“故宫”站或“景山东门”站下车。 · 地铁： · 地铁6号线“北海北站”B出口，步行约15分钟可达公园西门。 · 地铁8号线“中国美术馆站”A出口，步行约20分钟可达公园东门。 · 重要提示：故宫和景山周边区域交通管制严格，极难打车和停车，强烈建议乘坐公共交通工具前往。 --- 周边联游推荐 景山公园地理位置极佳，可以与周边多个著名景点串联游览： · 南面：紧邻故宫博物院，通常安排“故宫-景山”一日游。 · 西面：与北海公园一街之隔，可以顺路游览。 · 东面：不远处是王府井商业街，可以购物和用餐。 · 北面：穿过地安门大街可前往什刹海、南锣鼓巷等历史文化街区。 总结 景山公园以其独特的地理位置、丰富的历史内涵和极佳的观景视角，成为游览北京不可或缺的一站。它就像一位历史的守望者，静静地矗立在紫禁城背后，等待着游客登顶，去感受那份穿越数百年的帝都气韵。 希望这些信息能帮助您更好地规划行程！

北京景山公園 景山公園是元、明、清三代的御苑。坐落在北京城的中軸線上，西臨北海，南與故宮神武門隔街相望， 北面可以遠眺奧運公園紀念塔。公園中心的景山為堆土而成，全城的最高點。 很多人都去過故宮, 但都不知故宮真面貌。在景山公園萬春亭，就可以一睹故宮全貌。因為這裏就是[紫禁之巔 ]！可以清楚拍攝到神武門，故宮博物館出口。 唔講你可能唔知，北京城中心點 就在景山公園裏。絕對值得，去拍照，打卡留念。 該公園是國家AAAA級旅遊景區, 當然不只萬春亭能一睹故宮全貌， 這裏還是一個超大花園，同有很多古建築。 園內現有古松柏一千餘株，種植牡丹、芍藥等花卉幾萬株，三季花團錦簇，四季松柏常青。加上經常舉辦花卉、盆景展覽和各種文化活動，這座古老的皇家園林充滿了新時代的生機。 古建築有綺望樓、五方亭、壽皇殿、永思殿、牡丹園等景點。 這裏遊客不算多，一般都可以現場買票。當然最好就是網上預約啦！ 我最喜歡就是這裡的花卉，同古建築。因為遊客不多可以慢慢細心拍出有質素嘅照片。

京城之「紫禁之巔」景山公園散策~景山為一座人造山，遼金時稱「青山」，元稱「鎮山」，明改稱「萬歲山」，又明初朝廷在此山堆煤，以防元朝殘部圍困北京引起燃料短缺，遂又稱「煤山」，清則改稱「景山」。其西臨北海，南與故宮神武門隔街相望，是元、明、清三代的御苑，公園坐落在明清北京城的中軸線上，曾是京城的制高點，故又有「紫禁之巔」的稱號。從明思宗自縊處的景山東麓上山頂，先至周賞亭，再經觀妙亭，最後便到山頂的萬春亭，若從西麓則是先到富覽亭，再經輯芳亭便到山頂，山頂萬春亭可360度環景俯覽京城。南望可一覽紫禁城全景，北探可一俯壽皇殿與鼓樓，東視可直逼北京第一高樓中國尊，西瞰可直窺中南海與北海加上日薄西山。唐朝之劉禹錫曾有詩云: 「庭前芍藥妖無格，池上芙蕖淨少情。唯有牡丹真國色，花開時節動京城。」，如今園內遍植牡丹與芍藥，真有花開時節動京城之感。

If you want to get a glimpse of the entire Forbidden City and see the world’s largest group of palaces, you can see the entire Forbidden City as long as you go to Jingshan Park. It looks like a king over the world, so when you visit the Forbidden City, you just need to cross a road to the opposite side. When you come to the entrance of the Wansui Gate of Jingshan Park, after climbing the stairs up to Jingshan, you can overlook the Forbidden City below. The Forbidden City covered by white snow is very beautiful, and it feels like time has stopped. In addition, there are some historical stories. Jingshan is an artificial hill. From the Liao Dynasty, the soil from the Beihai was piled up here and became a small hill. The accumulation of various generations, especially the soil from the moat and the South China Sea in the Ming Dynasty, piled up into Wansui Mountain. In the early Ming Dynasty, the imperial court piled up coal here, so Jingshan is also called Meishan. 位於北京故宮北面的景山公園，是建於元朝將拆除元大都舊皇城的渣土，以及挖新紫禁城筒子河的泥土，堆積在迎春閣的舊址上，所形成一座人造土山，取名「萬歲山」，此地也就成為明大內皇宮北面的御園。 公園不算非常大，不過蠻清幽的，地處北京城中軸線最高點，位於故宮北側，是一座環境優美的皇家園林，紅牆環繞，園內松柏蔥鬱，古樹參天，登高遠眺，可俯瞰整個紫禁城！
